articles.title: Asian shares mostly fall and US futures are little changed after US inflation data improves
articles.description: Shares are mostly lower in Asia and U.S. futures are little changed after U.S. inflation data showed an improvement in July. U.S. stocks rose to a record. Oil prices were holding steady early Friday after slipping 2% on Thursday. On Wall Street, the S&P 500 climbed 0.7% and topped its prior all-time high set last week. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 0.1%, and the Nasdaq composite gained 0.8%. Treasury yields eased after a report showed inflation at the U.S. wholesale level was lower in July, at 4.7%. That was better than economists had expected and than the 5.5% rate for June.

articles.title: Rupee gains 2 paise to 95.43 against US dollar in early trade
articles.description: The rupee gained two paise against the US dollar in the early market hours, driven by a softening dollar internationally. Nonetheless, the outflow of foreign investments from Indian equities is weighing on the rupee's performance. Compounding this issue, rising crude oil prices linked to geopolitical conflicts further affected market sentiments, resulting in declines for the Sensex and Nifty in morning trading.

articles.title: Indian bond bias stays positive, debt auction demand in focus
articles.description: Indian government bonds remained firm in early trade on Friday. The benchmark 10-year bond yield held above the key 6.75% level. Investors awaited a weekly debt auction for fresh market cues. Lower oil prices and U.S. Treasury yields offered some support. India's overnight index swap rates dipped without strong trends.

articles.description: Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty declined in early trade on Friday as the prolonged US-Iran standoff kept investors cautious.
